```json
{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Adopt a feature-based Git branching strategy with one branch per user story, integrated through a release branch for the increment.",
    "Use the existing Spring Cloud Stream binder SPI (Channel, Binder, ProducerProperties, ConsumerProperties) as the extension point for the new Azure Event Hubs binder (U1).",
    "Implement U1 as a dedicated spring-cloud-stream-binder-eventhubs module, reusing Azure SDK for Java and following the pattern of the existing Kafka/Rabbit binders.",
    "For U2 (IPython Notebook), use the Apache Zeppelin-style kernel gateway approach via a Spring XD admin REST endpoint that exposes a code-evaluation channel, leveraging the Jupyter Kernel Gateway over WebSockets.",
    "U3 will be implemented as a Spring XD distribution-side migration utility (a one-shot script + admin CLI command) that backs up xd/config/*.yml and zookeeper data into a versioned directory before applying the upgrade.",
    "U4 (direct binding) will be implemented as a new 'direct' binder that uses in-process queues (or a per-JVM transport) instead of a broker, configurable via spring.cloud.stream.bindings.<ch>.binder=direct.",
    "U5 (xd-admin REST) will expose a REST controller over the existing xd-admin server, mapping HTTP verbs to the existing DeploymentManager and StreamRepository operations, returning DTOs (not domain entities) with proper status codes.",
    "U6 (ModuleRegistry stubs) will provide an in-memory ModuleRegistry implementation satisfying the ModuleRegistry interface so the rest of Spring Cloud Stream/Skipper can be tested without ZooKeeper/Redis.",
    "U7 will be executed as a multi-module Maven/Gradle repo migration: move the module artifacts and POMs from spring-cloud-stream-modules into spring-cloud-streams, update parent references, and publish new coordinates.",
    "U8 (in-memory stream repo) will be implemented as a Map-based @Repository that satisfies the StreamDefinitionRepository interface, enabled via a profile (e.g., 'in-memory') to override the default JDBC implementation.",
    "Java 17 baseline (per Spring 6.0 requirement) will be used for all new code; backporting to Java 8 is out of scope.",
    "Tests will use JUnit 5, Spring Boot test slices, Testcontainers where external systems are required, and Mockito for unit tests."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "A single experienced Java/Spring developer performs all activities; no team coordination overhead is included.",
    "Development environment, Azure subscription credentials, and a ZooKeeper instance are already available; provisioning is not included in the estimates.",
    "The existing Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, and Spring Cloud Data Flow codebases are familiar to the developer; no ramp-up learning time is included beyond minimal reference checks.",
    "U1, U2, U3, U4, U5, U6, U7, U8 are largely independent and can be developed sequentially by one person; some shared interfaces (e.g., ModuleRegistry) are refactored once and reused.",
    "The Azure Event Hubs Java SDK is stable and well-documented; no custom protocol reverse engineering is required.",
    "The IPython/Jupyter Kernel Gateway will be invoked as an external process, not embedded in the JVM.",
    "REST APIs in U5 follow standard Spring MVC conventions and do not require a new authentication mechanism beyond what xd-admin already provides.",
    "Module migration (U7) is purely a build/repo reorganization; no behavioral changes to the modules are required.",
    "Documentation is concise developer-facing reference docs (README, Javadoc) — not full user manuals.",
    "Effort estimates cover design, implementation, unit tests, and light integration tests; large-scale performance/load testing is excluded."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Overall architecture, design, and scaffolding",
      "activity_description": "Analyze the eight user stories, define integration points across Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, and Spring Cloud Data Flow, draft interface changes (ModuleRegistry, StreamDefinitionRepository, Binder SPI), set up multi-module project skeleton, and document the high-level design.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Azure Event Hubs binder (U1)",
      "activity_description": "Design, implement, and unit-test a new spring-cloud-stream-binder-eventhubs module including Producer/Consumer abstractions, partition mapping, checkpointing via Azure Blob Storage, and configuration metadata.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "IPython Notebook integration (U2)",
      "activity_description": "Add a kernel-gateway bridge in Spring XD admin, expose a WebSocket-based notebook endpoint, integrate with the existing shell/CLI to allow interactive data exploration against live streams and batch jobs, and write integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Spring XD upgrade mechanism (U3)",
      "activity_description": "Implement an upgrade CLI/utility that detects a previous installation, snapshots the config dir and servers.yml, applies the new distribution, and restores/merges the prior configuration with conflict handling and rollback support.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Direct module binding without middleware (U4)",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement a 'direct' binder that connects producers and consumers in-process using blocking queues, supports per-JVM delivery, and falls back cleanly when multi-JVM is requested. Include configuration properties and tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "xd-admin REST APIs for pipeline CRUD (U5)",
      "activity_description": "Expose REST endpoints (create, deploy, undeploy, list, destroy) for stream and batch pipelines on xd-admin, add DTOs, validation, error handling, HTTP status mapping, and integration tests against an embedded admin server.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "ModuleRegistry in-memory stubs (U6)",
      "activity_description": "Implement an in-memory ModuleRegistry implementation plus lightweight service-layer stubs so mock streams can be assembled and exercised via the registry API in tests and sample apps.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Migrate spring-cloud-stream-modules to s-c repo (U7)",
      "activity_description": "Move module POMs, source, and resources from the spring-cloud-stream-modules repository to the spring-cloud-streams (s-c) repo, update parent/dependency declarations, fix imports, and verify build and a smoke test of representative modules.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "In-memory stream definition repository (U8)",
      "activity_description": "Add a Map-backed StreamDefinitionRepository implementation, wire it under an 'in-memory' Spring profile, document usage, and add tests showing it works without an external store.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Integration and end-to-end testing",
      "activity_description": "Run cross-feature integration tests (e.g., REST API deploying a stream that uses the direct binder and the in-memory repository), fix regressions, and validate that the Azure Event Hubs binder connects to a real (or Testcontainer-ized) Event Hubs emulator.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Documentation",
      "activity_description": "Write README sections, Javadoc, configuration property reference tables, and short usage examples for each new feature (U1, U4, U5, U8); update the upgrade guide for U3; add a migration note for U7.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 320
  }
}
```

For U2 (IPython Notebook), use the Apache Zeppelin-style kernel gateway approach via a Spring XD admin REST endpoint that exposes a code-evaluation channel, leveraging the Jupyter Kernel Gateway over WebSockets.

U3 will be implemented as a Spring XD distribution-side migration utility (a one-shot script + admin CLI command) that backs up xd/config/*.yml and zookeeper data into a versioned directory before applying the upgrade.

U4 (direct binding) will be implemented as a new 'direct' binder that uses in-process queues (or a per-JVM transport) instead of a broker, configurable via spring.cloud.stream.bindings.<ch>.binder=direct.

U5 (xd-admin REST) will expose a REST controller over the existing xd-admin server, mapping HTTP verbs to the existing DeploymentManager and StreamRepository operations, returning DTOs (not domain entities) with proper status codes.

U6 (ModuleRegistry stubs) will provide an in-memory ModuleRegistry implementation satisfying the ModuleRegistry interface so the rest of Spring Cloud Stream/Skipper can be tested without ZooKeeper/Redis.

U7 will be executed as a multi-module Maven/Gradle repo migration: move the module artifacts and POMs from spring-cloud-stream-modules into spring-cloud-streams, update parent references, and publish new coordinates.

U8 (in-memory stream repo) will be implemented as a Map-based @Repository that satisfies the StreamDefinitionRepository interface, enabled via a profile (e.g., 'in-memory') to override the default JDBC implementation.
Java 17 baseline (per Spring 6.0 requirement) will be used for all new code; backporting to Java 8 is out of scope.
Tests will use JUnit 5, Spring Boot test slices, Testcontainers where external systems are required, and Mockito for unit tests.
assumptions: A single experienced Java/Spring developer performs all activities; no team coordination overhead is included.
Development environment, Azure subscription credentials, and a ZooKeeper instance are already available; provisioning is not included in the estimates.
The existing Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, and Spring Cloud Data Flow codebases are familiar to the developer; no ramp-up learning time is included beyond minimal reference checks.
U1, U2, U3, U4, U5, U6, U7, U8 are largely independent and can be developed sequentially by one person; some shared interfaces (e.g., ModuleRegistry) are refactored once and reused.
The Azure Event Hubs Java SDK is stable and well-documented; no custom protocol reverse engineering is required.
The IPython/Jupyter Kernel Gateway will be invoked as an external process, not embedded in the JVM.
REST APIs in U5 follow standard Spring MVC conventions and do not require a new authentication mechanism beyond what xd-admin already provides.
Module migration (U7) is purely a build/repo reorganization; no behavioral changes to the modules are required.
Documentation is concise developer-facing reference docs (README, Javadoc) — not full user manuals.
Effort estimates cover design, implementation, unit tests, and light integration tests; large-scale performance/load testing is excluded.

activities.activity_description: Analyze the eight user stories, define integration points across Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, and Spring Cloud Data Flow, draft interface changes (ModuleRegistry, StreamDefinitionRepository, Binder SPI), set up multi-module project skeleton, and document the high-level design.

Design, implement, and unit-test a new spring-cloud-stream-binder-eventhubs module including Producer/Consumer abstractions, partition mapping, checkpointing via Azure Blob Storage, and configuration metadata.

Add a kernel-gateway bridge in Spring XD admin, expose a WebSocket-based notebook endpoint, integrate with the existing shell/CLI to allow interactive data exploration against live streams and batch jobs, and write integration tests.

Implement an upgrade CLI/utility that detects a previous installation, snapshots the config dir and servers.yml, applies the new distribution, and restores/merges the prior configuration with conflict handling and rollback support.

Design and implement a 'direct' binder that connects producers and consumers in-process using blocking queues, supports per-JVM delivery, and falls back cleanly when multi-JVM is requested. Include configuration properties and tests.

activities.activity_name: xd-admin REST APIs for pipeline CRUD (U5)
activities.activity_description: Expose REST endpoints (create, deploy, undeploy, list, destroy) for stream and batch pipelines on xd-admin, add DTOs, validation, error handling, HTTP status mapping, and integration tests against an embedded admin server.
Implement an in-memory ModuleRegistry implementation plus lightweight service-layer stubs so mock streams can be assembled and exercised via the registry API in tests and sample apps.

Move module POMs, source, and resources from the spring-cloud-stream-modules repository to the spring-cloud-streams (s-c) repo, update parent/dependency declarations, fix imports, and verify build and a smoke test of representative modules.
Add a Map-backed StreamDefinitionRepository implementation, wire it under an 'in-memory' Spring profile, document usage, and add tests showing it works without an external store.

Run cross-feature integration tests (e.g., REST API deploying a stream that uses the direct binder and the in-memory repository), fix regressions, and validate that the Azure Event Hubs binder connects to a real (or Testcontainer-ized) Event Hubs emulator.
Write README sections, Javadoc, configuration property reference tables, and short usage examples for each new feature (U1, U4, U5, U8); update the upgrade guide for U3; add a migration note for U7.
